A case relies on such an entry when it runs under a `None` or unknown dialect and its outcome comes from that entry. It also relies on one when, under any dialect, its outcome differs from the `None`-dialect outcome only because the entry is in the union. An example is a `sqlite_`-prefixed data table under dialect `mysql` that proves the configured dialect arrives, as in the MySQL row #382 gave `test_with_widgets_hides_introspection_result_under_configured_dialect`. Naming ChromaDB's `chroma.sqlite3` file is not a use. A use is *SQLite-only* when the behaviour it asserts exists only for SQLite. That covers at minimum: the `sqllens.agent.integrations.sqlite` package, `sqlite_path_from_url` and `_readonly_uri`; the SQLite preflight probe; a `sqlite`-keyed entry of a per-dialect table in `src/sqllens/safety/` or in the system prompt (for example `sqlite_master`, `pragma_*` names, `load_extension`); `sqllens init`'s SQLite template; `claude-desktop install`'s SQLite file-stem naming; a case that relies on a SQLite entry of the fallback union; and a `sqlite` case whose expected outcome differs from the same test's `mysql` case with the same other inputs. A use whose classification is unclear counts as SQLite-only, and its test also gets a MySQL version. A `sqlite` URL used only as the non-MySQL input that a MySQL-only check refuses (`tests/unit/test_rule_set_file.py::test_non_mysql_url_is_refused`, `tests/unit/test_cli_rule_sets.py::test_validate_refuses_a_non_mysql_url`) is engine-neutral where another non-MySQL scheme can reach that check: its replacement passes one, for example `postgresql://u@db.invalid/shop`, straight to `load_rule_sets`, and asserts the same refusal. Instrument: coverage.py, installed with `pip install coverage` for the measurement only, `python -m coverage run -m pytest -q`, then `python -m coverage json`, comparing each file's `executed_lines` under all of `src/sqllens/`. Every line that the merge base's default run executes is also executed by this branch's default run with the map's `SQLite-only` tests deselected. Lines are matched through the PR's diff of `src/`: a line the diff deletes needs no match, and every line the diff adds that coverage.py reports as a statement (in `executed_lines` or `missing_lines`) is executed. The one exception is a line that no non-SQLite input can execute. It is defined by where the code is, not by which tests ran: a line in `sqllens.agent.integrations.sqlite` or `sqllens.preflight._probe_sqlite`, or a line inside a branch whose condition holds only for the `sqlite` dialect, a URL whose scheme starts with `sqlite`, or a SQLite database file, or a line in a function whose every caller is such a line (for example `sqllens.safety.relations._sqlite_kind`). When it is unclear whether a line is such a line, a MySQL test executes it. The PR body states the merge-base SHA compared against, and lists each excepted line as `path:line` or a line range with the SQLite-only condition that guards it.
